faq.a: Transmission of securities is the process by which ownership of shares, mutual fund units, or other investments is passed from a deceased investor to their legal heirs.

faq.q: What is the difference between physical and demat holdings?
faq.a: Physical holdings refer to shares held as paper certificates. Demat holdings (short for dematerialised) are shares held electronically in a demat account, which is like a bank account for securities.

faq.q: What kind of "simplified documentation" is needed now?
faq.a: Typically, this might include a death certificate, a copy of the will (if any), an affidavit, a no-objection certificate (NOC) from other legal heirs, and an indemnity bond. The exact list can vary but is significantly less cumbersome than full court processes.

faq.q: How quickly can the process be completed now?
faq.a: While SEBI has simplified the rules, the actual time taken can still depend on the completeness of documents and the efficiency of the Depository Participant or Registrar and Share Transfer Agent. However, the aim is to complete the process much faster than before, especially with the Quick Transmission Processing for smaller amounts.

faq.q: Does this apply to all types of investments?
faq.a: These rules primarily apply to listed shares and other securities like mutual fund units. For other assets like property or bank accounts, different rules apply, though the general principle of simplifying inheritance is gaining traction across various financial sectors.
